sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the manna was a food of hunger, alluding to the inner dimension of Torah which, being knowledge of existence rather than grasp of essence, creates a hunger to attain the essence.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is stated in the Midrash,
that the manna was a food of hunger.
For the explanation of “And He caused you to hunger… the manna” is that “He caused you to hunger” refers to “the manna,”
that the manna caused you to hunger.
And the concept is,
that manna alludes to Aggadah
[as it is written,
“And it was like coriander seed, white,” and it is stated in the Mechilta, “like an Aggadah that draws a person’s heart,”]
which is
the innerness of the Torah.
And as explained in many places,
that “bread from the earth” is the revealed aspect of Torah,
and “bread from the heavens”
(manna)
is the innerness of the Torah.
And since in the innerness of the Torah there is only knowledge of existence and not comprehension of essence,
therefore,
the study of the innerness of the Torah is connected with hunger
(in the manner of “hunger to hear the word of G-d”)
to attain the essence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes two aspects within the innerness of Torah—one related to the intellect connected to the emotions (bread from the earth within pnimiyus) which satisfies, and one above the emotions (bread from the heavens within pnimiyus) which is a food of hunger because it is not grasped.

translations.translation: And on a deeper level, it can be said that what the Midrash states, that the manna is a food of hunger,
the intention in this is
(not only that the manna does not negate hunger in the person who eats it,
but also)
that the manna itself is a food of hunger.
And this will be understood by prefacing that the above explanation, that “bread from the earth” is the revealed aspect of Torah and “bread from the heavens” is the innerness of the Torah,
is in general,
but in particular,
these two matters
(“bread from the earth” and “bread from the heavens”)
exist also within the innerness of the Torah.
And the concept is,
it is stated in Tanya
that in the study of the innerness of the Torah there are two matters.
That it is a “lofty mitzvah”
and exalted, and that it brings to a perfect heart.
And it can be said,
that the study of the innerness of the Torah, since it brings to a perfect heart,
because it pertains to the matter of clarifications
(clarification of the emotions),
is similar to “bread from the earth,”
and the primary matter of “bread from the heavens” is in the study and knowledge of the innerness of the Torah in its own right.
And it can be said,
that the distinction between these two modes of study is also in the level of the intellect.
For the study and knowledge of the innerness of the Torah in order to come to a perfect heart is in the intellects that are related to the emotions,
and the study and knowledge of the innerness of the Torah in its own right is in the intellects that are above the emotions.
And based on this, it can be explained that the manna is a food of hunger,
for the matter of satiety
(in the matter of intellect)
is that it grasps the intellect,
therefore,
the knowledge and comprehension of the intellects related to the emotions
(“bread from the earth” within the innerness of the Torah)
which is grasped in a person’s intellect in actual comprehension and grasp
(therefore this comprehension also affects his emotions)
is a food that satisfies,
and the knowledge and comprehension of the intellects that are above the emotions
(“bread from the heavens,”
manna)
which is in a manner of wondrous concealment and is not grasped
(so much)
in a person’s intellect,
is a food of hunger.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between two interpretations of "food of hunger"—one where the knowledge is relative to the emotions and causes hunger in the person, and another where the knowledge itself is a level of hunger above the emotions, leading to self-nullification, analogous to the distinction between Chochmah and Binah and the hunger of Yom Kippur.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the distinction between the two interpretations of “food of hunger”—
that it does not negate hunger in the person, and that the food itself is a hunger that is above grasp
(even though the knowledge that causes hunger in the person is also because it is above his comprehension)—
is,
that this knowledge is on the level of intellect that is relative to the emotions,
except that it is above them,
and therefore it causes in the person
(whose essence is emotions)
hunger and thirst to attain the matter.
And the knowledge that itself is a level of hunger,
is on the level of intellect that is above the emotions
(as above, section 2),
therefore,
it is a level of hunger in essence relative to the emotions.
And when this level is revealed within the emotions,
they are in a state of self-nullification.
And this is analogous to the distinction between Chochmah and Binah,
that through the comprehension of Binah,
when the contemplation and comprehension is in the wondrous concealment of the Ein Sof that is above worlds,
it brings to a great love
(in yearning and thirst),
there is one who loves,
and through the vision of Chochmah he comes to awe,
self-nullification.
Nevertheless, even this level of manna is called a “food of hunger,”
for the refinement that comes through eating the manna is that the person who eats the manna is utterly nullified,
and through this he becomes
(like)
a vessel to receive vitality from a light that is not proportionate to him.
And this is analogous to the matter of “to give them life through hunger”
of Yom Kippur,
that the hunger of Yom Kippur is a level of essential, imperceptible delight that is above eating and drinking
[and as is known,
that the reason Yom Kippur is forbidden in eating and drinking is because on Yom Kippur there is a revelation of essential, imperceptible delight],
and the matter of “to give them life through hunger” is that on Yom Kippur they receive vitality from this delight.
